prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on your injuries, the complexity of the claim, where the crash happened, the insurance situation, and whether you want a lawyer who will try your case in court if needed.

How to find the best attorney for your case
- Look for experience with car-accident and bodily-injury claims (preferably catastrophic/injury type that matches yours).  
- Trial experience and a record of significant settlements/verdicts — not just small claims.  
- Resources to investigate (medical experts, accident reconstructionists).  
- Good client communication: clear fee agreement, regular updates.  
- Contingency-fee representation (you pay only if they recover money).  
- Strong local reputation: peer reviews, verdicts, and client reviews (Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, AVVO, Google reviews).  
- Transparency about fees, expected timeline, and strategy.

Well-known Chicago firms often recommended for car-accident/personal-injury work
(you should interview a few and pick the best fit):
- Clifford Law Offices — known for catastrophic car-accident and wrongful-death representation.  
- Power Rogers & Smith, P.C. — plaintiff personal-injury firm that handles car crashes.  
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard P.C. — plaintiff-focused personal-injury litigation.  
- Goldberg Weisman Cairo — handles serious personal-injury claims in Chicago.

(These are examples of established Chicago firms; there are many other capable attorneys and smaller firms that may be an excellent fit.)

Questions to ask at a free initial consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?  
- Will you or a specific attorney handle my case? (Get that attorney’s contact.)  
- Do you try cases or generally settle? How many trials have you handled in the last 3–5 years?  
- What are your fees and costs? (Typical contingency fee, who pays expenses if we lose?)  
- What is your estimate of my case’s value and timeline?  
- How will we communicate (email, phone), and who’s my primary contact?

Red flags
- Vague answers about experience or results.  
- Pressure to sign immediately.  
- No written fee agreement or unwillingness to explain costs.  
- Poor communication during the initial call.

Practical next steps
- If you want, tell me: the date/location of the crash, severity of injuries, whether fault/insurance is admitted, and your ZIP code — I can produce a short, tailored list of Chicago attorneys with practice areas and links to reviews so you can set up consultations.  
- Keep in mind Illinois’ statute of limitations for most personal-injury claims is two years from the date of injury, so don’t delay contacting an attorney.
